angry.context: An angry face with lowered brows. Used for angry reactions, complaints and bad-experience ratings, frustration in feedback forms and chat stickers.

confused.context: A confused face with a wavy mouth. Used for 'I don't understand' reactions, help or FAQ prompts, unclear results and feedback about confusing content.

cool.context: A face wearing sunglasses. Used for cool or chill reactions, confident and relaxed moods, summer themes and approval in chat.

cry.context: A crying face with a tear. Sad reactions, disappointment and hurt feelings, failed actions in playful interfaces and mood tracking use it.

grimace.context: A grimacing face showing clenched teeth. Used for awkward or oops moments, embarrassment and cringe reactions, and nervous 'yikes' replies in chat.

heart-eyes.context: A smiling face with hearts for eyes. Used for love and adoration reactions, favourite items, dating apps and very positive ratings.

kiss.context: A face blowing a kiss with a small heart. Common in messages of love and affection, thank-you and goodbye reactions, dating apps and Valentine's content.

laugh.context: A laughing face with squinting eyes and an open grin. Used for funny reactions, jokes and humour sections, lol replies in chat and happy ratings.

nerd.context: A nerdy face with round glasses and buck teeth. Used for geeky or smart reactions, study and education apps, tech topics and playful know-it-all replies.

neutral.context: A neutral face with a straight mouth. Fits the middle option in ratings and satisfaction surveys, meh reactions and no-strong-feelings mood entries.

party-face.context: A face in a party hat. Used for celebrations, birthdays and anniversaries, finished goals or milestones, and festive reactions in chat.

poop-emoji.context: A smiling swirl of poop. Used for silly and joking reactions, joke ratings, potty training apps and pet waste reminders.

relieved.context: A relieved face with calm, closed eyes. Shows relief after a finished task, calm and content moods, phew reactions and wellbeing check-ins.

sad.context: A sad face with a frown. Used for bad or low ratings, error and empty states, disappointment reactions and mood trackers.

sick.context: A face wearing a medical mask. Used for feeling ill, sick days and health status, flu season or infection notices, and masked reactions in chat.

skull-emoji.context: A cartoon skull with big eye sockets. Used for 'I'm dead' laughing reactions, spooky and Halloween themes, game over screens and dark humour.

sleepy.context: A sleeping face with closed eyes and a Z. Used for tired moods, bedtime and sleep tracking, idle or away status and boring-content reactions.

smile.context: A simple smiling face. Happy reactions and good ratings, satisfaction surveys, friendly greetings and emoji pickers use it.

star-struck.context: A grinning face with stars for eyes. Used for amazed and excited reactions, fan moments, top content picks and very high ratings.

surprised.context: A surprised face with an open mouth. Used for shock and wow reactions, unexpected results, surprise announcements and chat stickers.

thinking.context: A thinking face with a raised brow and a hand on its chin. Used for 'let me think' reactions, questions and doubt, processing states in playful interfaces and quiz apps.

tongue-out.context: A face sticking out its tongue. Used for silly or cheeky reactions, jokes and teasing, playful kids' content and yummy food moments.

wink.context: A winking face with one eye closed. Common in playful or joking replies, hints and inside jokes, flirting and friendly chat reactions.

worried.context: A worried face with raised brows. Used for concern and anxiety in mood trackers, nervous reactions, gentle warnings and mental health check-ins.

zipper-mouth.context: A face with its mouth zipped shut. Used for secrets and confidential content, mute or quiet modes, no-spoilers notices and 'my lips are sealed' replies.
